transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. I've just been having a bit of a hard time lately. It's probably nothing major, I know you see people with much worse problems, but... I came in because I just can't seem to shake this... this certainty that I'm being punished. 

It's about my father. I feel like I let him decline, and... I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds strange to say out loud, and I really don't want you to think badly of me. But even when my sister tries to comfort me, you know, she shows me the doctor's notes or she tells me I've done everything right... it doesn't change it. It just feels like some sort of terrible judgment has already been passed on me. 

Is... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has this sense of punishment or judgment been present every day, most of the day, for at least two weeks?

Well, I really hope I'm not wasting your time with all this, but... it's been going on for a little while now. About a year and two months, I think? It started right around the time my father's health and behavior really started changing, and I had to step into more of a caregiving role for him. 

As for it being every day... I mean, I try so hard to push it down and just be pleasant for everyone else. You kind of have to keep a smile on at work, especially in HR. But... yes, if I'm being completely honest, that heavy feeling of being punished is there most of the day, pretty much every day. Definitely for the last two weeks, and probably a lot longer. I'm sorry, I know I probably should have come in and asked for help sooner. Did... did that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure or feel interested in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

Oh, um... well, I try really hard to stay active and engaged, I promise. I don't want to be a downer for anyone else. But... to be completely honest, I guess I have noticed a bit of a change. 

I used to really love gardening on the weekends, and going to brunch with my sister. And lately... I don't know, I just haven't had the energy for it. I'll still go if she asks, of course, because I don't want to disappoint her, but... I'm just kind of going through the motions. I don't feel that spark of joy I used to get from it. Even at work, which I usually enjoy... it just feels so hard to care about the employee relations issues right now. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible, like I'm just giving up. I really am trying to push through it. Is... is it normal to feel that way? I hope I'm not sounding too negative.
Have you felt guilty or blamed yourself for things more than you think is reasonable, especially regarding your father's situation?

Oh, um... well, I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself. My sister tells me that all the time. I really do try to look at things objectively, like I would for one of my employees at work. But... 

I just... I keep going over every little decision I've made about my father's appointments. And then I think about every tense conversation I've had with my relatives about his care, and... I don't know, I just end up feeling like I'm this incredibly selfish daughter. And it spills over, too—I feel like a completely useless employee lately because my mind is always on this. 

I just feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me because of how badly I've handled everything. I'm sorry, I know that's probably an overreaction, and I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party for myself. I try to keep it together, I promise. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed by these feelings that you've thought about hurting yourself or wished you were not alive?

Oh, gosh. Um... I really don't want to alarm you, and I promise I'm not a danger to myself or anything. I don't have a plan to do anything like that. I really try to stay strong for my dad and my sister. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest, there are times when it just feels so heavy. Sometimes... I catch myself thinking that it would just be so much easier if I didn't wake up at all. Especially on those mornings when I know I have to deal with more calls from the home care agency, and then I have to log on and face all the employee issues waiting for me at work. It just feels like too much sometimes. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's a terrible thing to say, and I feel awful even admitting it. I really am trying to push past those thoughts. Is it... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or feel tired all the time, even after getting enough rest?

Oh, um... actually, no, I don't think so. I really try my best to keep my energy up, you know? I make sure to push through and keep moving so I don't let anyone down at work or with my dad. 

I mean, I might have normal tiredness at the end of a long day, but if I get enough sleep, I usually feel pretty okay physically. I'm definitely not just lying in bed all day, I promise. I always make sure to get up and get ready for the day. 

I hope that's a good sign? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information... is it okay if I haven't really noticed that one?
Have you noticed that it's been harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Oh, um... well, I really try to stay on top of everything. I have to, right? With my dad's care and my job in HR, people are always depending on me to have the answers. 

I mean, maybe I take a little longer to read through an email sometimes, or I might double-check a schedule just to be absolutely sure... but I really think that's just me trying to be thorough. I wouldn't say I can't focus or think clearly. I still get all my work done, and I make all the decisions for my dad's appointments. I promise I'm not dropping the ball on anything important. 

I just... I want to make sure I'm doing everything right. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope it's okay that I haven't really had trouble with that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep — like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Oh, um... well, sleep is... I mean, I wouldn't say I'm sleeping more than usual. Definitely not that. I try really hard to keep a normal schedule. 

But, um... I guess falling asleep can be a little tricky sometimes. I just... I want to make sure I handled everything right during the day, you know? So I end up kind of replaying all the phone calls with the home care agency, or second-guessing the care decisions I made for my dad. Just trying to be thorough, really. So sometimes it takes me a little while to finally drift off. 

And then... well, I have been waking up a bit early. Usually around 3 or 4 in the morning. And my chest just feels so tight, like I'm already behind on the day before it even starts. I try so hard to go back to sleep, I really do, but I just can't seem to turn my brain off before I have to get up for work. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be managing my stress better so I can sleep. I'm really trying. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you had times when you felt like your mind just went blank or that you couldn’t think clearly, even when you tried hard to focus?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say my mind goes blank. I really try to stay sharp, you know? With everything I have to juggle at work and with my dad, I can't really afford to just zone out or lose my train of thought. 

I mean, I might have a moment where I pause to collect my thoughts, but I think everyone does that, right? Especially when things are busy. I always manage to pull it together and figure out what needs to be done. I'm definitely still able to think through problems and get my tasks finished on time. 

I really hope that's okay to say. I just want to be honest that I'm still functioning well in that area. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately — like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I try very hard to make sure I'm eating properly. I know I have to keep my energy up for work and for my dad, right? You can't pour from an empty cup, as they say. 

So I always make sure to have my meals. Maybe sometimes I'm a little rushed and just grab something quick, like a salad or a sandwich at my desk, but I definitely haven't lost any weight. My clothes all fit exactly the same as they always have. 

I really do try to be responsible and take good care of myself in that department. I hope it's okay that everything is pretty normal there... I'm definitely making sure I eat enough. Is that... does that give you what you needed to know?

Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (F66.0) is included due to the focus on responsibility and guilt. Psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia (F20.x) are considered due to the patient’s concern about judgment and internal experience, though there is no clear evidence of delusions or hallucinations yet.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.12) remains possible but less likely given the duration and severity. Psychotic disorders (F20.x) and paraphilias (F66.0) are ruled out due to absence of psychotic features or relevant clinical context.

The patient's persistent guilt, anhedonia, and self-blame, along with the duration of symptoms exceeding one year, continue to support the differential of Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent, Severe (F33.3) and complicated grief or adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.12). The initial episode possibility (F32.3) remains considered due to the chronicity and lack of clear remission periods described.

The patient reported persistent guilt, anhedonia, and self-blame, which supports major depressive episode (F32.3) or recurrent depressive disorder (F33.3). The absence of a prior episode makes F32.3 more likely, but F33.3 remains a candidate if there is a history of a previous episode not yet confirmed. F43.12 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood) is ruled out due to the duration and severity of symptoms exceeding adjustment disorder criteria.

The patient continues to endorse key depressive symptoms including persistent guilt, rumination over past decisions, anhedonia, and early morning awakening with distressing thoughts. The absence of psychomotor retardation and significant fatigue does not strongly support melancholic features, keeping both current candidates viable. No new information sufficiently rules out either F32.3 or F33.3.
